newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swissair says intercontinental demand rose.
newsitem.headline: Swissair says intercontinental demand rose.

text.p: Swissair AG said a 9.2 percent increase in the demand for its flights in 1996 mainly came from growth on intercontinental routes, just like in 1995.
Demand, or revenue tonne-kilometres, on Swissair's intercontinental routes rose 10.6 percent in 1996, while supply, or available tonne-kilometres rose 10.9 percent, the airline said in a statement.
Overall, Swissair's revenue tonne-kilometres rose 9.2 percent to 3.84 bilion. Supply, or available tonne-kilometres, rose 9.5 percennt to 5,54 billion.
The overall load factor for 1996 was 69.2 percent, slightly down from 1995's 69.4 percent.
Including Crossair AG, the other airline in the SAirGroup, overall available tonne-kilometres rose 10.9 percent and revenue-tonne kilometres rose 10.2 percent.
Together Swissair and Crossair transported a total of 10.36 million passengers, an increase of 6.7 percent. In addition, one million charter passengers were transported.

Demand for Swissair's South Atlantic routes was favourable, rising 31.6 percent in 1996, largely due to the introduction of a fourth weekly flight. Last year Swissair resumed its service to Rio de Janeiro via Sao Paulo.
Far Eastern routes saw a growth of 16.1 percent, followed by an increase of 8.1 percent, Africa by 1.4 percent and the Middle East by 0.1 percent.
In Europe, available tonne-kilometres rose 3.2 percent, but demand was only up by 0.4 percent.

"This descrepancy was largely due to the introduction of a new timetable concept in November of last year, which resulted in a significantly higher number of seats becoming available at one time," Swissair said.
Experience shows, Swissair said, that demand takes longer to catch up with such an increase in availability.
